summary: v24/v20 materially improve the release DAG, Linux control primitives, fork-safe process graph, authenticated child attestation, legacy-worker staging and archive continuation. But the executing inner runtime is not yet self-bound to the RuntimeCandidate named by Pin/Policy, and the M6 6/44 authority prefix is not mechanically bound through the observed live ledger snapshot into staged worker bytes. Immutable rejection-slot conflicts and P1 liveness/cancellation also remain unresolved deterministic recovery decisions.
commands: read-only inspection of v24/v20, frozen threat model, gate/contract, raw worker, historical M6 verifier and current trial ledger

limitations: No project-code execution, training, archival replay, budget consumption, real PIT certification, or final-OOS access.

blockers: Introduce an observed inner-runtime capability and exact RuntimeClosure/AuthorizedEntrypoint equality before Bootstrap/PASS/E/C.
Define a 6/44 ledger authority-prefix to observed snapshot to staged-ledger byte-equality chain that tolerates legitimate atomic ledger replacement without accepting legacy 4/29 inputs.
Resolve occupied-malformed archive rejection slots without overwriting immutable evidence or pretending a canonical rejection was published.
Define P1 idle/worker deadlines, cancellation/reap and pre-lock teardown before tests or implementation.
Reissue architecture and change design, then obtain fresh independent R3 design reviews before test design, implementation, replay, M7 or final-OOS work.
